How should the impression be handled?
options: Treat it as high risk and refuse to send it
Send it untreated with a warning label
Standard precautions: rinse, disinfect per protocol, label and send, as for every patient
questions.why: Standard precautions for every patient.

questions.stem:
A rigid five-unit bridge from 13 to 17, with a pier at 15, has debonded at 13. There is caries under the 13 retainer.
What is the most appropriate management?
options: Cut the bridge and leave 13 untreated
Remove it, treat the caries, and redesign with a non-rigid connector at the pier or as separate bridges
questions.answerText: Remove, treat, redesign at the pier.
questions.why: Remove, treat, redesign at the pier.

questions.stem:
A crown on 11 looks too light. The shade was taken after preparation under the operating light.
What explains the mismatch?
options: Dehydration and poor lighting; the shade should be taken before preparation in colour-corrected daylight
questions.why: Dehydration and poor lighting.

questions.stem:
A patient with moderate haemophilia A needs several extractions before an immediate upper denture.
What is the most appropriate management?
options: Proceed in practice with local measures only
Liaise with the haemophilia centre, avoiding regional blocks without factor cover
questions.why: Haemophilia centre liaison.

questions.stem:
A 68-year-old has taken oral alendronate for 2 years for osteoporosis, without steroids. A tooth under her RPD needs extraction.
What is the most appropriate approach?
options: Proceed with standard care and no drug holiday; review healing
questions.why: Standard care, no drug holiday. Low-risk MRONJ profile.

questions.stem:
A patient with a severe gag reflex has never tolerated an upper complete denture.
Which option may help?
options: An implant-retained palateless prosthesis (after referral), with desensitisation
questions.why: Implant-retained palateless prosthesis.

questions.stem:
A patient asks whether her resin-bonded bridge has been a "success" because it is still present after 6 years, though it has debonded twice.
What is the most accurate explanation?
options: It has survived, but success means in place and free of complications
questions.why: Survived, not a success.

questions.stem:
A 30-year-old has lost 12. 13 is sound, unrestored and enamel-rich, and the occlusion is light.
What is the most appropriate first-choice replacement?
options: A conventional fixed-fixed bridge from 11 to 13
questions.why: Single-wing resin-bonded cantilever.

questions.stem:
A patient with an upper complete denture and only lower anterior teeth has a flabby premaxilla and enlarged tuberosities.
What is the most appropriate management?
options: Provide posterior support with a lower RPD, and use a selective-pressure impression for the flabby ridge
questions.why: Posterior support and selective pressure. That manages combination syndrome.

questions.stem:
A 74-year-old attends for a denture adjustment and mentions new pain in the jaw when chewing, a headache and scalp tenderness.
What is the most appropriate action?
options: Adjust the denture and review in a month
Same-day medical referral for suspected giant cell arteritis
questions.why: Same-day referral for suspected GCA.

questions.stem:
A patient had a myocardial infarction 3 weeks ago and asks to start elective bridgework now.
What is the most appropriate approach?
options: Liaise with the physician and defer elective treatment until he is medically stable
questions.why: Liaise and defer elective care.

questions.stem:
A patient on dual antiplatelet therapy needs a crown preparation with retraction cord.
What is correct?
options: Continue both antiplatelets; it is a low bleeding-risk procedure
questions.why: Continue antiplatelets.

questions.stem:
A 66-year-old smoker has an ulcer under her lower denture flange that persists 4 weeks after the flange was adjusted.
What is the most appropriate action?
options: Adjust further and review in 3 months
Urgent referral on the suspected cancer pathway
questions.why: Urgent suspected cancer referral.

questions.stem:
An audit showed incomplete RPD prescriptions. The practice introduced a template.
What is the next step?
questions.why: Re-audit.

questions.stem:
A patient has completed treatment with an implant overdenture, a Co-Cr RPD and several crowns.
What is the most appropriate long-term plan?
options: Review only when there is pain
Risk-based recall with supportive periodontal and peri-implant care, prosthesis maintenance, and recording of patient-reported outcomes
questions.answerText: Risk-based recall with maintenance and PROMs.
questions.why: Risk-based recall with maintenance and PROMs.
